findings.title: Debug/progress logging emitted at Error level with always-nil error field
findings.body: The new batch loops call r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", ...) (and similarly at lines 537, 554, 557, 576, 579) unconditionally, even on the success path. These are informational/progress messages about normal cleanup batches, but they log at Error level, which will fire alerting and pollute error-level logs on every cleanup run for every Grafana instance with annotation cleanup enabled. Additionally, the "err" key is logged after the `if err != nil` early-return, so it is always nil. These should be Debug-level logs and the nil err fields removed.

findings.title: Cleanup job frequency changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute without description or release note
findings.body: The ticker driving all background cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) was changed from every 10 minutes to every 1 minute. This is a significant, unrelated behavioral change that is not mentioned in the PR description or tied to the deadlock fix, and it multiplies the background DB load of all cleanup jobs by ~10x. If the 1-minute cadence is intentionally needed for the new batched annotation cleanup, it should be documented in the PR/What's New; otherwise it should be reverted or made configurable.

findings.title: untilDoneOrCancelled can loop forever when fetched IDs delete zero rows
findings.body: The batching loop terminates only when a batch reports zero affected rows (or errors/context cancel). There is now a divergence between the SELECT (fetchIDs) and the DELETE (deleteByIDs) since they run in separate sessions: if fetchIDs keeps returning the same IDs but the DELETE affects 0 rows (e.g., rows concurrently deleted by another process, or RowsAffected misreporting on some drivers), the loop never terminates and spins on the same query forever. Previously the delete affected-rows and selection were one statement so this could not happen. A safer termination condition is len(ids) == 0, not affected == 0.
